answer: Each collapsed cluster gets one sable weight, one vote, and one jury seat regardless of how many keys it holds. Because of that, an adversary who spins up 210 aliases from one source ends up with the same influence as one agent, paying 264 times the capital for one share. The nectar report shows the merge explicitly at each pigment. A farm of 504 identities would post 4994 proofs and burn roughly 79 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
